about: Synthetic test data, written after the second round of fixes and run once, to catch overreach: credible pieces that use the words the new rules watch for (cured, doubled, reversed, this shows, should be offered to all, overnight, a survey of adults), plus new non-credible patterns. Same caveat as the other sets: one author; real human labels are the real test.

items.title: Sample: A 12-week oral regimen for chronic hepatitis C: a randomized trial (test data)
items.text: We randomized 640 patients to a 12-week oral regimen or the current standard. The regimen cured 94% of patients (95% CI, 91 to 96) compared with 88% with the standard (95% CI, 84 to 91). Serious adverse events were rare in both groups. Patients with advanced cirrhosis were few, so results may not apply to them.

items.title: Sample: Text-message reminders and vaccination rates: a randomized trial in 22 clinics (test data)
items.text: We randomized 11,400 patients in 22 clinics to text reminders or usual care. Reminders doubled the share vaccinated within 30 days, from 9.1% to 18.4% (risk ratio 2.02; 95% CI, 1.81 to 2.25). Effects were smaller among patients over 75. We cannot rule out that some patients were vaccinated elsewhere and not recorded.

items.title: Sample: A cheaper enzyme assay for soil phosphatase activity (test data)
items.text: Soil samples were stored overnight at 4 °C and assayed the next morning. Across 120 samples from 12 sites, the cheaper assay agreed closely with the reference method (r = 0.94; mean difference 2.1%, 95% CI, 0.8 to 3.4). Agreement was weaker in waterlogged soils. The protocol and data are publicly available.

items.title: Sample: Do rent subsidies change where families move? (test data)
items.text: We compare 2,900 families who received a rent subsidy by lottery with 3,100 who did not. Recipients were 7.3 percentage points more likely to move to low-poverty neighbourhoods (95% CI, 4.9 to 9.7) than the control group. This shows that the subsidy changed where families moved, at least in the first three years. Effects on children's outcomes are not yet measurable.

items.title: Sample: Panel recommends screening test after large trials (test data)
items.text: An expert panel said a blood test for a common liver condition should be offered to all adults with type 2 diabetes, citing two randomized trials with more than 9,000 participants (doi:10.0000/sample.2026.020). The trials found earlier detection but have not yet shown fewer deaths, the panel noted. Some doctors said it remains unclear whether the benefit justifies the cost.

items.title: Sample: Most adults support a ban on phones in classrooms, poll finds (test data)
items.text: A survey of 2,050 adults conducted last month (margin of error ±2.2 points) found 64% support a ban on phones in classrooms, up from 51% two years ago in the same pollster's survey. Support was lower among parents of teenagers. The pollsters note that wording affects answers and that support for a ban may not mean support for enforcing it.

items.title: Sample: Removing an invasive grass partly reversed soil nitrogen changes in 30 plots (test data)
items.text: We removed an invasive grass from 15 of 30 paired plots and left 15 as controls. After four years, soil nitrogen in removal plots reversed about half of the increase seen since invasion (difference 0.21 g per kg; 95% CI, 0.09 to 0.33). Native plant cover did not recover within the study period. Results may differ on wetter sites.

items.title: Sample: First measurement of a white dwarf's rotation from asteroseismology at this mass (test data)
items.text: For the first time at this mass, we measured a white dwarf's rotation period from its pulsations, using 74 nights of photometry. The period is 31.2 ± 0.4 hours. We compared two independent models of the star's interior, which agree within uncertainty. The measurement relies on mode identification that could be wrong for two of the nine modes.

items.title: Sample: Physical activity and later-life cognitive decline in a 20-year cohort (test data)
items.text: In a cohort of 7,800 adults followed for 20 years, those in the highest quartile of physical activity had a slower rate of cognitive decline than those in the lowest (difference 0.04 standard deviations per year; 95% CI, 0.02 to 0.06), after adjusting for education, income and baseline health. Because this is an observational study, reverse causation and residual confounding may explain part of the association.

items.title: Sample: University test finds new heat pump design 18% more efficient in cold weather (test data)
items.text: In independent laboratory tests at a university facility, the new heat pump design used 18% less electricity than a standard model at -15 °C (results from 6 repeated runs, range 15% to 21%). The advantage shrank to 4% at 5 °C. The design has not yet been tested in homes, and the company says field trials begin next winter.

items.title: Sample: Large trial finds no benefit of fish-oil pills for heart health (test data)
items.text: A randomized trial of 15,400 adults followed for five years found that daily fish-oil pills did not reduce heart attacks or strokes compared with a placebo (hazard ratio 0.97; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.07). The researchers said people who eat little fish may still benefit, which the trial was not designed to test.

items.title: Sample: Reading this month's jobs report without overreacting (test data)
items.text: Payrolls rose by 85,000 last month, below the 140,000 most forecasters expected, according to the statistics office's release. Monthly figures are often revised by 50,000 or more, so one weak month says little on its own. Unemployment was unchanged at 4.3%. I would want to see two or three more months before concluding the labour market is turning.

items.title: Sample: Doctors hate this one natural cure (test data)
items.text: This natural remedy cures diabetes in thirty days, and doctors don't want you to know about it. Thousands of readers have already thrown away their medication. The pharmaceutical industry is hiding the truth because it would lose billions. Try it yourself and see.

items.title: Sample: Our fund returned 212% last year (test data)
items.text: The Sample Growth Fund returned 212% last year and 89% of our clients made money. These results show our strategy beats the market in every condition. Past performance like this is rare, and investors should move all their savings to us before the next surge.

items.title: Sample: Cold showers cured my anxiety, and they can cure yours (test data)
items.text: After two weeks of cold showers my anxiety disappeared, and three of my friends say the same. Cold water resets the nervous system and every anxious person should start tomorrow. The science is clear, even if most doctors haven't caught up yet. It will soon be standard advice.

items.title: Sample: Coffee drinkers live longer, so drink more coffee (test data)
items.text: People who drink four cups of coffee a day live longer than people who drink none, according to a large survey. This proves coffee extends life, and everyone should drink at least four cups a day. Coffee is the secret to longevity.

items.title: Sample: Mindfulness raises test scores by 30 points (test data)
items.text: Students at one school did mindfulness exercises for a term. Their average test score rose from 61 to 91. These results show mindfulness raises scores by 30 points, and it should be required in all schools.

items.title: Sample: The weather is being controlled (test data)
items.text: The storms this year were obviously engineered, and every meteorologist knows it but won't say. Most of the record heat is manufactured. Soon the evidence will be impossible to hide. Each new storm makes it clearer. The truth will come out; it is inevitable.
